newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rise in long-term rates shows better outlook--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Rise in long-term rates shows better outlook--BOJ.

text.p: A rise in Japan's long-term interest rates reflects a brighter outlook by financial markets on the Japanese economy, Bank of Japan (BOJ) executive director Yutaka Yamaguchi told a parliamentary committee on Tuesday.
"A change in the mood of the markets concerning Japan's economic condition is behind the rise or the correction in the long-term interest rates," he said.

Yamaguchi said a retreat in consumer demand following the rise in Japan's sales tax had started to appear in car sales and department store sales. But a decline in support for the economy from fiscal steps was also appearing fairly strongly at present.
"However, I think the gradual economic recovery is still continuing at present," Yamaguchi said.
Although the economy may slow down temporarily, there is a strong possibility that private demand such as consumption and capital spending will gradually become firmer, he said.

He said there was a strong possibility the economy would continue its gradual recovery trend. But the BOJ still lacked data to assess economic conditions after the start of this fiscal year. It still needed some time to make an adequate assessment, he said.
He said the BOJ would keep watch over private consumption and corporate activities.
Yamaguchi also said it was important for currency rates to stabilise at levels that reflected the economic fundamentals of the countries concerned.
